solution:
Number the columns 0 through 9 from west to east. On the full grid, a path consists of 9 east steps and 3 south steps, so choosing the positions of the south steps gives \(\binom{12}{3}=220\) paths.
The missing edges are at columns 4 and 5, both on the middle south step (the second of the three). If that step is at column \(k\), the first south step can be in any column from 0 to \(k\), and the last in any column from \(k\) to 9. These columns determine the path uniquely, giving \((k+1)(10-k)\) paths. The two forbidden cases are disjoint, so the valid count is \(220-5\cdot6-6\cdot5=160\).
Final answer: 160
